newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Concha says Ecuador still studying Convertibility.
newsitem.headline: Concha says Ecuador still studying Convertibility.

text.p: Ecuador is still studying the possibility of adopting currency "Convertibility" under which the sucre would be pegged to the dollar, Finance Minister Pablo Concha told Ecuadorean television Monday.
Ecuador's new President Abdala Bucaram has pronounced himself in favor of revaluing the sucre to give it strength against the dollar.

"This project announced by the president is being studied and could be considered as part of the changes in economic plans the country demands," Concha said, describing the idea as "a stable relationship to the dollar over coming years."
The minister said Ecuador would thus depend on strict fiscal discipline and export growth to gain in efficiency, eliminating its dependency on monetary measures.
"The government will have to create the right conditions for this process to have the success it had in Argentina, Hong Kong and other countries," Concha said.
Domingo Cavallo, the former Argentine economy minister who created his country's successful Convertibility Plan in 1991, is now one of Bucaram's chief economic advisors.
Opponents of Ecuadorean Convertibility argue that it would be unsustainable because Ecuador does not have high enough levels of capital inflows, reserves or price stability.
The sucre is currently quoted at about 3.3 to the dollar.
